kill_fact: The bear case's Europe pillar is already falsified by the very report the record is dated after. The record asserts Europe is 'the clearest instance of narrative running ahead of numbers', that a second-half return to growth 'has not yet appeared', and that it is 'the oldest unverified claim in the file'. On the 29 July 2026 second-quarter call - five days before the record's as_of date of 4 August 2026 - EMEA net sales were $484 million, UP 2% year on year and down only 2% organically, against down 29% organically in the March 2026 quarter and down 14% in the December 2025 quarter. That is a 27-point organic swing in one quarter, reported growth already positive, and the third-quarter guide sets EMEA at mid- to high-teens organic growth. The claim that 'the number went the other way' was true through March 2026 and is not true on the tape the record is built on.
corrections: (1) EUROPE - MATERIAL. Correct 'Europe has not returned to growth / the number went the other way' to: EMEA net sales $484m in Q2 2026, +2% reported and -2% organic (from -29% organic in Q1 2026), with Q3 2026 guided to mid- to high-teens organic growth and the full year to low-single-digit organic growth (Q2 2026 call, 29 July 2026). The claim is stale by one quarter relative to the record's own as_of date. (2) BACKLOG BLACKOUT - OVERSTATED, not wrong. The disclosure fact verifies exactly: on 11 February 2026 management said 'the best approach is to no longer report actual orders, orders forecast or backlog with quarterly earnings', with full-year backlog retained only in the Form 10-K; the 29 July 2026 call gave no backlog figure and no book-to-bill. But the bear's stronger claim - that the leading indicator is now 'visible once a year' and that every pipeline claim since February is 'unaudited management assertion' - does not survive. Deferred revenue is on the face of the filed quarterly balance sheet, management named it on 29 July 2026 as 'a read through in terms of those advanced deposits on orders', and it went from $1,814.7m at 31 December 2025 to $2,461.8m at 31 March 2026 to $3,633.7m at 30 June 2026 - a doubling in six months and +$1.17bn sequentially in Q2 alone. That is a filed, auditable, quarterly order-intake proxy, and it points up. (3) SOP_BEAR ARITHMETIC - MINOR. The adverse case's own parts are $41.20 (service) + $85.20 (product) - $0.40 (net debt) = $126.0 a share, not the $128 stated as the total; recomputed from the underlying blocks ($16.2bn + $33.5bn less $146m over 393m diluted shares) it is $125.8. bear_px corrected to 126.0. Also note the adverse case's own revenue base of $14.5bn ($2.7bn service + $11.8bn product) is described as 'roughly flat with 2026' but is 3.6% ABOVE the $14.0bn now guided for 2026 - the downside case is fractionally less adverse than it presents itself. (4) WHAT SURVIVES INTACT, verified against primary sources: gross margin 32.16% in Q2 2025 ($848.5m/$2,638.1m) to 37.71% in Q2 2026 ($1,234.9m/$3,274.3m) - the trajectory claim is exact, not asserted from a proxy; net debt $145.6m at 30 June 2026 (total debt $3,256.2m including $316.4m of finance leases, less $2,810.6m cash and $300.0m short-term investments) - the $146m figure is right and FMP's headline $445.6m is the version that omits short-term investments; the fiscal 2022 precedent is real (net income $76.6m, free cash flow -$263.8m); the $118.70 twelve-month low and $379.94 high are real; 41.9x trailing EV/EBITDA on $2.524bn TTM EBITDA is arithmetically correct at $273.35. No hidden funding disqualifier found: diluted shares 389.8m to 392.7m year on year (+0.7%, stock compensation only), no equity raised, capex funded inside a $2.5bn free-cash-flow guide.

evidence: Vertiv Q2 2026 earnings call, 29 July 2026 (CFO Craig Chamberlin): 'In EMEA, net sales were $484 million up 2%, with organic sales down 2%. We continue to see a strengthening market, which supports our position for the region to return to organic sales growth in the second half of 2026.' Same call, Q3 2026 guidance: net sales $3.75bn midpoint, organic growth approximately 35%, 'By region, we expect Americas organic growth in the high 30s, APAC in the high 30s, and EMEA in the mid- to high teens'; full year raised to $14.0bn, 31% organic, adjusted EPS $6.65-$6.75, adjusted free cash flow $2.5bn. No backlog figure and no book-to-bill were given.

Vertiv Q1 2026 earnings call, 22 April 2026: 'Turning to EMEA. Net sales were $321 million, down 29% organically' - confirms the record's baseline, and confirms that the Q2 print is a 27-point organic improvement rather than a continued deterioration.

Vertiv Q4 2025 earnings call, 11 February 2026 (CEO Giordano Albertazzi): 'Our book-to-bill ratio was 2.9x. Our backlog stands at $15 billion, more than double last year's', fourth-quarter organic orders 'up 252% year-over-year'; and 'we believe that currently, the best approach is to no longer report actual orders, orders forecast or backlog with quarterly earnings... We will continue to provide our full year historical disclosure regarding sales and backlog in our Form 10-K.' The bear's disclosure-withdrawal fact and its 11 February 2026 date both verify.
